_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The Rayonier Advanced Materials Pulp Mill is located at 4470 Savannah Highway, Jesup, Wayne County, Georgia.  This facility remains a three-mill, Kraft pulping complex involved in the manufacture of bleached dissolving pulp.  

This report is being submitted to satisfy the EPA 5-year RMP resubmission requirements. Since the previous RMP update there has been no change associated with the General Manager's position.  The contacts of the RMP Preparer, Emergency Contact, and Site Contact of the plant has been updated.  

This updated RMP report outlines a summary of the changes made to the Chlorine Dioxide (Program Level 3) covered process and communicates the elimination of Sulfur Dioxide (also a Program Level 3) to be no longer used at the Jesup mill as a bleaching agent.

In 2023, the Jesup plant completed a project to upgrade the SVP (Single Vessel Process) ClO2 Supply Pumps and Lines from Kynar-lined to Titanium, including:
     * Demolishing five (5) A/B ClO2 supply pumps
     * Installing two (2) new ClO2 supply pumps (one of which is a spare) inside the current ClO2   
        Storage containment area
     * Demolished four (4) 2" existing Kynar-lined supply lines
     * Installed a new 8" supply line
     * Installed VVFD on pressure control for new ClO2 supply pumps.

In 2024, the Jesup plant initiated a project to install a ClO2 heat exchanger to improve the efficiency of the chlorine dioxide plant. As part of the management of change process, a chlorine dioxide PHA review was conducted as part of the design review.  

Also In 2024, The Jesup plant operations eliminated the purchase of sulfur dioxide delivered by rail to the mill for use in pulp bleaching operations. As a result, sulfur dioxide is no longer used within the mill for bleaching purposes and is no longer applicable to reporting upon within this Risk Management Plan.  Sodium Bisulfite (CAS# 7631-90-5) is not considered an RMP applicable chemical. 

1. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency R

esponse 
The Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies remain essentially unchanged with the exception of removing reference to the use of Sulfur Dioxide for bleaching purposes. 

2. Facility and Regulated Substances Handled
The RYAM Jesup Pulp Mill remains a three-mill, Kraft pulping complex involved in the manufacture of bleached dissolving pulp located in Wayne County, Georgia. The only RMP applicable chemical used onsite is chlorine dioxide.  

3. Prevention Program
The Rayonier Jesup Pulp Mill exceeds the threshold quantity for the OSHA Process Safety Management (PSM) Standard, 1910.119, for chlorine dioxide, therefore this process remains subject to both PSM and RMP Level 3 requirements. 

The Rayonier Jesup Pulp Mill has a program in place to comply with the OSHA Process Safety Management Standard, 29 CFR 1910.119. It includes a preventative maintenance plan which requires all PSM covered equipment to be periodically inspected and serviced. This will ensure that the equipment remains in good operating condition and will minimize the probability of accidents due to faulty equipment. 

As part of the  PSM Program, the facility maintains written operating procedures for the PSM covered pulping processes. These procedures cover all phases of operation and include information on safety devices. These procedures are used to train all operators and mechanics who work on the PSM covered pulping processes to ensure consistency of operation and minimize human error. These measures help to ensure that all operators and mechanics are properly trained. Existing safe work practices such as Lockout/Tagout and Hot Work Permit, are periodically reviewed and updated to ensure that all non-routine work can be performed safely.
Other components of the prevention program include collection and periodic review of all process safety information, including Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs). The staff ensures that if equipment design deficiencies are ident

ified that they are corrected. These actions will ensure that the equipment meets industry standards and that accurate process safety information will be available when needed.

To ensure that Rayonier Jesup Pulp Mill staff has the skills necessary to identify unsafe conditions, they are included in a training program. The training program includes an overview of the process, hazards of the process, (eg. Process Hazards Analyses), Operating Procedures, Maintenance Procedures, Emergency Response, and Safe Work Practices. 

The Rayonier Jesup Pulp Mill staff working in conjunction with a risk management consultant conducted a PHA of the chlorine dioxide process initially in 1996, prior to startup, and revalidations have been performed since then at the required intervals. Additional PSM procedures, including Management of Change, Pre-Startup Safety Review, Compliance Audits, and Incident Investigation also ensure the continued safe operation and prompt correction of deficiencies. The PSM Program receives full support of plant management and involvement of employees at all levels.

4. Five-year Accident History
The Rayonier Jesup Pulp Mill  has had no accidental releases of covered chemicals that have resulted in offsite consequences in the past five years.

5. Emergency Response Program
The Rayonier Jesup Pulp Mill has written Emergency Procedures in place. The site also has internal emergency response capability and has developed a program to comply with paragraph (q) of 29 CFR 1910.120. The current plan has been coordinated with the Wayne County Emergency Management Agency. 

6. Plans to Improve Safety 
The Joint Safety and Health Committee continues to provide the Jesup Mill with tangible safety improvements primarily based on active participation and suggestions from employees.
The use of a incident management system (IMS)is used to track action items relating to incident investigations, PHA recommendations, and audit findings.  Most importantly, incidents are inv
estigated to determine root cause and appropriate corrective actions.  Learnings from many of these investigations are shared with others throughout the company.
